quality_guards: Suitable controls depend on the actual surface, contaminant, weather, lighting, traffic and users at the location.
Slip and trip guidance is workplace-context evidence and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
The safe method depends on load size, shape, grip, posture, frequency, route and the individual worker.
Manual-handling evidence is task- and person-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
Required action depends on measured daily or weekly exposure, peak sound pressure, duration and the actual work pattern.
Occupational-noise guidance is exposure-specific context and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
Manufacturer vibration values alone may not represent exposure in the actual task, tool condition and material.
Vibration evidence is tool-, task- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
The correct controls depend on the substance, route of exposure, concentration, process, duration and affected workers.
COSHH evidence is substance- and process-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
Whether the pressure-system regulations apply depends on the equipment, relevant fluid, pressure and specific exclusions.
Pressure-system evidence is equipment- and operating-condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
Safeguarding must match the actual machine, access needs, failure modes and residual risks; generic guarding is not sufficient.
Machinery-safety evidence is equipment- and task-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
Assessment and equipment needs depend on the individual, workstation, work pattern and whether work is at home, in an office or hybrid.
DSE evidence is workstation- and user-specific and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
